shortcut_name: small terminal set enables subset Steiner DP
evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses "full = (1 << t) - 1" and "initialisation: single terminal sets"; glm-5 explicitly branches on "if t <= 1" and computes distances between critical nodes
removal_suggestion: The terminal-count bound cannot be removed under the immutable-element restriction. Instead, re-present the routing requirement so that a valid connection cannot freely use arbitrary noncritical intermediate buildings—for example, explicitly require every selected route to use only audit-critical buildings as internal vertices.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Exponential subset dynamic programming over the at-most-ten audit-critical buildings, combined with shortest-path relaxation
Metric-closure computation between critical buildings followed by terminal-subset optimization

common_affordance: The audit-critical set has at most ten vertices, making a 2^t terminal-subset algorithm feasible

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The submitted implementation contains an invalid/incomplete loop fragment, shown as "for k i", so its Floyd-Warshall-based approach cannot execute correctly.

It models the task as an MST/Kruskal problem via "find_mst_with_critical_nodes", which can select unnecessarily expensive edges instead of using noncritical Steiner buildings to connect the critical vertices optimally.

recommended_edit: Because the numeric terminal bound is immutable, target the next shared semantic affordance: replace "possibly passing through other intermediate buildings" with a requirement that connections between audit-critical buildings may not freely use arbitrary noncritical buildings as internal vertices.
regression_risk: Restricting routes to audit-critical endpoints could make the problem an ordinary MST on the critical subgraph, potentially restoring the defeated Kruskal/MST solution from qwen3-coder.
